Less than three months before the midterms, and things are getting ugly.

   Sen. Jon Ossoff (D., Ga.), running for re-election in November, tore into President Trump in a weekend speech.

   “He doesn’t want to do the job,” Ossoff said of Trump on Sunday. “He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the emir of Qatar.”

   Of all the things Ossoff said, one word stood out: Natalie.

   He was speaking of Natalie Harp, who is perhaps Trump’s closest aide. She is constantly by his side, tapping out social-media posts for him, fetching information for him. She was one of the few people who joined him during the secret Air Force One switcheroo in Turkey last month.

   The ferocity with which the White House swung back is reflective of the lengths Trump will go to in order to defend Harp.

   “Instead of denigrating hard working people serving their country, Jon should look deep into his soul and ask himself why he’s a miserable person who hates this country,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung  posted on social media Monday.

   Asked about Ossoff’s comments by a reporter Monday, Trump responded, “You mean Pee-wee Herman?”

   Harp has long been devoted to Trump, and she has credited him with saving her life. She spoke at the 2020 GOP convention and said a 2018 law known as “Right to Try,” enacted by Trump, gave her access to treatment for her bone cancer. She is now one of the most important White House staffers that few people outside Washington know about.

   Have Democrats struck a nerve by adding her to a Trump attack? Name-calling and the like is a game that Trump often plays, but how far will Democrats go? White House Aide Natalie Harp Is at Center of Messy Brawl
 
Plus, the attorney general launches a process for felons to reclaim their gun rights, and Trump allies flock to Iowa
 
 
AARON SCHWARTZ/AFP/GETTY IMAGES
 

Good morning. Less than three months before the midterms, and things are getting ugly.

 

Sen. Jon Ossoff (D., Ga.), running for re-election in November, tore into President Trump in a weekend speech.

 

“He doesn’t want to do the job,” Ossoff said of Trump on Sunday. “He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the emir of Qatar.”

 

Of all the things Ossoff said, one word stood out: Natalie.

 

He was speaking of Natalie Harp, who is perhaps Trump’s closest aide. She is constantly by his side, tapping out social-media posts for him, fetching information for him. She was one of the few people who joined him during the secret Air Force One switcheroo in Turkey last month.

 

The ferocity with which the White House swung back is reflective of the lengths Trump will go to in order to defend Harp.

 

“Instead of denigrating hard working people serving their country, Jon should look deep into his soul and ask himself why he’s a miserable person who hates this country,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung posted on social media Monday.

 

Asked about Ossoff’s comments by a reporter Monday, Trump responded, “You mean Pee-wee Herman?”

 

Harp has long been devoted to Trump, and she has credited him with saving her life. She spoke at the 2020 GOP convention and said a 2018 law known as “Right to Try,” enacted by Trump, gave her access to treatment for her bone cancer. She is now one of the most important White House staffers that few people outside Washington know about.

 

Have Democrats struck a nerve by adding her to a Trump attack? Name-calling and the like is a game that Trump often plays, but how far will Democrats go? The Atlanta Journal-Constitution has an interesting headline on its Ossoff story: “Jon Ossoff Wants More Than a Win Against Mike Collins.” He’s on the national stage now.

 

This is an edition of the Politics newsletter, bringing you an expert guide to what’s driving D.C. every day. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

People and Policies I’m Watching

 

Primary elections: Voting takes place Tuesday in Florida, Alaska and Wyoming.

 

White House ballroom: Tuesday is the deadline in the Supreme Court for plaintiffs to file their response brief to challenge the White House’s emergency appeal over the ballroom.

 

Trump’s Tuesday: The president is scheduled to hold policy meetings throughout the day.

What I’m Following

 
 
ELIZABETH FRANTZ/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

Attorney General Todd Blanche is launching a process to restore felons’ gun rights. Individuals who lost their gun rights because of felony convictions will be able to apply to have them reinstated. People convicted of violent crimes won’t get their firearms back, but a host of felony offenders, who were facing gun bans for life, will now have a pathway to become gun owners again.

 

Trump allies are flooding Iowa to bolster shaky Republicans ahead of the midterms. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were perhaps the highest-profile officials to visit the Hawkeye State in recent days. Nonpartisan analysts rate the state’s race for governor and two of its four U.S. House contests as tossups either party could win.

 

Trump again threatened to bomb Oman if it ‘gets in the way.’ The president lashed out at Muscat on Monday over suspicions the U.S. partner in the Middle East is helping Iran tighten its grip on the Strait of Hormuz. For a second time this year, Trump warned Washington would bomb the Gulf country if it scuttled nuclear negotiations with Iran.

 
 
 

What Else Is Happening

 

• Trump told Israel to stop striking Gaza as Jared Kushner met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

 

• The head of Space Force told the WSJ how the U.S. uses space to fight wars on Earth.

 

• A New York state court judge has pushed back a scheduled September start date for Luigi Mangione’s murder trial.
